answer: Sybil resistance can come from stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a small refundable deposit before joining a market, and peers rate each completed job. Like a falcon that only trusts a lure it has seen work, the network weights ratings from long-lived, high-stake agents far more than fresh accounts. A velvet-smooth onboarding stays open to newcomers, but a sable-dark trail of failed jobs and slashed deposits follows every identity, so creating many fake agents costs more than the fraud earns.
